nodes.label: Voice pack library — six archetypes

nodes.label: Pack Failure mode field
nodes.rationale: Every voice has a degenerate form (operator-brief becomes military parody, playful-consumer becomes cringe, calm-expert becomes corporate mush, editorial-premium becomes beautiful emptiness). A pack that names its own overshoot makes it checkable in the audit instead of a matter of opinion; the library is harmful without it.

nodes.label: brand_lint.py
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only like ux_lint.py and ux_doctor.py; the linter checks only what a machine can prove and everything evaluative goes to the audit. --fix applies only changes that cannot be wrong; exit 0 clean, 1 warnings, 2 errors.

nodes.label: Sources: scan-surface declaration
nodes.rationale: The linter cannot guess where a project keeps its text, so a missing Sources: block is an error (B006): it refuses to report a clean run over a surface it never read. Checks whose source is absent are counted as skipped, never silently passed.

nodes.label: B030 — number in public copy absent from facts.md
nodes.norm_label: b030 — number in public copy absent from facts.md

nodes.label: B060 — AI-marker density in marketing documents
nodes.norm_label: b060 — ai-marker density in marketing documents

nodes.label: B061 — no humor, exclamation or emoji on loss surfaces
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable across all packs including playful-consumer, because on error, destructive-confirm and billing surfaces the user is losing data or money. Enforced by the linter rather than left to taste.
nodes.norm_label: b061 — no humor, exclamation or emoji on loss surfaces

nodes.label: SEO/AEO safety versus optimization split
nodes.rationale: Safety (stuffing, filler, clickbait mismatch, blocked crawlers, unearned superlatives, missing byline) is always on and machine-enforced; optimization (answer front-loading, evidence density, tables, schema, per-engine differences) is on request inside copywriting.

nodes.label: Absolute prohibition on fabricated facts
nodes.rationale: A hard fail, not a score reduction. The Princeton GEO work (KDD 2024) showed a lift from fabrication against GPT-3.5 in 2023, but it is now trained on as an adversarial signal, creates FTC §5 exposure, and the lift evaporates under competition (C-SEO Bench, NeurIPS 2025); real evidence in the same structural pattern captures 80-90% of the effect with none of the risk.

nodes.label: Humanization guards
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from the humanizer methodology, the only surveyed skill treating de-AI-ing as measurable engineering: S1/S2/S3 severity, an A-D grade on the result rather than the input, a 50% change-rate guard, a mandatory semantic-preservation self-check, and a density threshold above which patching is futile.

nodes.label: ux-audit scope copy
nodes.rationale: A new single-pass scope rather than a new skill: it judges what the linter cannot prove — tone drift, the 'could this sit on any other SaaS page' test, so-what failures, unproven claims, narrative coherence, pack failure-mode detection, register mismatch — with file:line evidence and the existing verdict vocabulary.

nodes.label: PRN-24 the interface never jokes about the user's loss
nodes.norm_label: prn-24 the interface never jokes about the user's loss

nodes.label: Topology B — two skills split by verb
nodes.rationale: brand-voice defines, copywriting produces, plus a copy scope inside the existing ux-audit. The hard boundary is that copywriting never writes to docs/brand/: a missing term or fact is reported, never invented to close a gap.
nodes.norm_label: topology b — two skills split by verb

nodes.label: One-way dependency: brand derives from foundation
nodes.rationale: The pack derives from foundation.md; the foundation never changes because a tone was appealing. With no foundation, brand-voice runs degraded, stamps Derived-from: inferred and recommends building the WHY layer first instead of blocking.
nodes.norm_label: one-way dependency: brand derives from foundation

nodes.label: Brand voice hard rule in CLAUDE.md
nodes.norm_label: brand voice hard rule in claude.md

nodes.label: Register deltas never cross invariants
nodes.rationale: A surface may move the five axes — a Reddit post can be longer, CTA-free and self-deprecating — but a brand that does not hedge does not hedge there either.

nodes.label: Registry adoption cost on legacy projects
nodes.rationale: An inventory sweep on a large product yields hundreds of B022 findings, so B022 is a warning rather than an error: only strings the team has agreed become blocking, and the hard rule is installed by the user's action rather than silently.

nodes.label: /brand-lint command
nodes.rationale: A clean linter means checkable, not good — the command is required to say so and offer the audit; with no docs/brand/ it routes to /brand-init rather than linting an absence.

nodes.label: /brand-update command
nodes.rationale: A rename must propagate to terminology.md, strings.md and every locale in the same change — a rename landing in one file and not the others is how two spellings start. A positioning change may deserve a different pack rather than a patched one.

nodes.label: /brand entry point
nodes.rationale: Inspect -> silent repair -> status -> menu with exactly one recommended action; the user is never asked to choose between skills or files, because that vocabulary is internal.

nodes.label: Brand routing table (user words to action)
nodes.norm_label: brand routing table (user words to action)

nodes.label: /copy command
nodes.rationale: First action is reading the pack; no pack means stop and route to /brand-init rather than improvise a voice. Copy is delivered before the reasoning, with two or three headline/CTA options and what each trades away.

nodes.label: /ux-audit command
nodes.rationale: Depth deep runs all five passes (scenarios, flow conformance, heuristics PRN, practices per the selection protocol, chain coverage); single-pass scopes run just that pass.

nodes.label: /ux-foundation command
nodes.rationale: After any change, the cascade check lists scenarios tracing to changed IDs and hands them to ux-scenarios in the same session.

nodes.label: /ux-lint command
nodes.rationale: Errors are drift or broken structure that must not merge; warnings are gaps to close. Recommended for CI or pre-commit so drift cannot merge silently.

nodes.label: /ux-update command
nodes.rationale: A new feature idea is validated against the chain first — an idea serving no job is challenged, not silently accepted; a change already made runs the Update workflow against the git diff and cascades to flows, screens and Figma links in the same change.

nodes.label: brand-voice skill
nodes.rationale: Owns docs/brand/ and never deviates from the contract's file, field and status names because the linter and the audit key off them. Invoked with no task it reports status and proposes exactly one next action.

nodes.label: brand-voice workflows: Init, Calibrate, Update, Validate
nodes.norm_label: brand-voice workflows: init, calibrate, update, validate

nodes.label: Voice derives from what the user loses on failure
nodes.rationale: The deciding input from the foundation is the stakes: a voice that charms when the stakes are a playlist is intolerable when the stakes are payroll.
nodes.norm_label: voice derives from what the user loses on failure

nodes.label: Degraded mode (Derived-from: inferred)
nodes.rationale: With no foundation the skill stamps the provenance as inferred, says plainly that the WHY layer should be built, and continues rather than blocking.

nodes.label: Inventory sweep into strings.md
nodes.rationale: Routes, screens, buttons, states, errors and empty states each get a row with file:line and the scenario served; parallel Explore subagents are dispatched one area each for a large codebase.

nodes.label: copywriting skill
nodes.rationale: Reads the pack first every time; guessing a voice and being wrong costs more than the pause, and copy invented surface by surface is exactly the drift this layer exists to remove. It never writes to docs/brand/.

nodes.label: Seven editing sweeps
nodes.rationale: Clarity, voice and tone, so-what, prove-it, specificity, emotion, zero risk — run in order with a loop back after each, but delivered prioritized by impact rather than reading order.

nodes.label: Adapt mode
nodes.rationale: What survives adaptation is the claim and the proof; length, structure, CTA policy and register change. A thread is not a page with line breaks, and each version must state what it drops.

nodes.label: Humanize mode
nodes.rationale: Text that already reads naturally is left alone; editing what is fine to prove the pass ran is this mode's failure.

nodes.label: copywriting non-negotiables
nodes.rationale: No fabricated facts under any framing; no humor on error, destructive confirm, billing or paywall surfaces in any pack; one action keeps one name (a second name is a defect, not a synonym); never quote a number absent from facts.md.

nodes.label: Naturalness grade A-D on the result
nodes.rationale: Graded after the rewrite rather than on the input, so the pass is measured by what it produced.
nodes.norm_label: naturalness grade a-d on the result

nodes.label: Machine-drafting markers catalog
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary, hedging chains, uniform 18-22 word sentences, identical paragraph shape, the rule-of-three habit, em-dash reflex, false balance, summary conclusions, symmetrical headings, over-signposting. Banned words are replaced with the thing they stood in for, never merely deleted; the fix for uniform length is rhythm, not vocabulary.

nodes.label: Vagueness where a fact belongs (S1)
nodes.rationale: 'Many companies', 'studies show', 'significantly improved' each mark a place where a specific claim was avoided because a specific claim can be checked. Replace with the real figure or say plainly there is none — honest absence beats confident vagueness, and this is the B030 rule from the other side.

nodes.label: Density threshold (~10 markers per 500 words)
nodes.rationale: Polishing a piece that is mostly patterns yields the same patterns with better words; saying so and rewriting from the argument is part of the job, not a failure of it.

nodes.label: Change-rate guard (over 50% do not ship)
nodes.rationale: Above half changed it is no longer an edit; it may be the right rewrite, but that is a decision with an owner, and quietly replacing someone's text while calling it a polish is how meaning gets lost unnoticed.

nodes.label: Semantic-preservation checklist
nodes.rationale: Numbers, dates, currency and proper nouns exact; causal direction unchanged; no negation inverted; quotations untouched; core claim and conclusion unchanged; register not drifted upward; every claim still traceable to facts.md. A failure means fix and re-check, not note and proceed.

nodes.label: What 'human' is not
nodes.rationale: Not typos, slang or deliberate roughness. The target is a person who writes well — with a position, specific knowledge and a reason to have written this — and friction is added only where a real writer would have it.

nodes.label: Tag → BP-id index (82 tags, 206 practices)
nodes.rationale: Makes finding practices cheap without deciding what is mandatory — that stays with the selection protocol.

nodes.label: bp_index.py generator + drift validator
nodes.rationale: The index is generated, never hand-edited; the validator fails when index and catalog disagree, and --stale reports Checked-date ages so they are not baked into a generated file.

nodes.label: BP tag taxonomy (stage/mechanism/domain/channel/craft/verbal/components)
nodes.rationale: Tags are the retrieval axis: filter by tag, open only matching entries, because reading the whole 1500-line catalog to find three practices is a real cost.

nodes.label: BP-001 Adapt competitor tactics, don't copy them
nodes.rationale: The one practice that ALWAYS applies; it is the anti-cargo-cult anchor — a practice is adopted only when it serves a traced job/story of THIS product.
nodes.norm_label: bp-001 adapt competitor tactics, don't copy them

nodes.rationale: A rule older than its review date is a hypothesis, not a constraint; a rule with no date cannot be audited, only believed.

nodes.rationale: Distilled from Apple HIG, Material Design 3, W3C ARIA APG and the GOV.UK Design System — the rule above all is to reach for the platform's standard component before inventing one.

nodes.label: Every interactive component ships all its states
nodes.rationale: Default is not a component; missing states are how PRN-01/PRN-09 silently fail, so the audit checks the state set and Figma variants must carry them.
nodes.norm_label: every interactive component ships all its states

nodes.label: Cross-platform stance (component of record, native before ARIA)
nodes.rationale: Pages carrying ARIA measure worse than pages without it, because every role is behavior the author must then implement by hand.
nodes.norm_label: cross-platform stance (component of record, native before aria)

nodes.rationale: The MCP gates its main tools behind guidance skills and skipping them is the most common cause of hard-to-debug failures; a missing MCP never blocks the chain, it degrades to markdown and syncs later.

nodes.label: Which Figma MCP tool for which job
nodes.rationale: Treat the list as a map, not a contract: if a tool is missing in the user's setup, degrade to what is there and say so — never invent a call.
nodes.norm_label: which figma mcp tool for which job

nodes.label: The Figma design loop inside ux-flows Design
nodes.rationale: The pack supplies the values, the visual-craft practices are the floor those values must clear; the compliance table then records those BPs as applied with the Figma frame as evidence.
nodes.norm_label: the figma design loop inside ux-flows design

nodes.label: Figma sync rule and boundaries (a rendering, never a replacement)
nodes.rationale: Flows, screens and scenarios remain the source of truth; a frame that drifts from its screen record is a finding, and the screens.md registry is the index that makes drift checkable.
nodes.norm_label: figma sync rule and boundaries (a rendering, never a replacement)

nodes.label: Names ARE the index (1:1 Figma ↔ super-ux IDs)
nodes.rationale: Every Figma object is named to match a super-ux ID so lookup is deterministic — no hunting, no guessing; that is the whole navigation model.
nodes.norm_label: names are the index (1:1 figma ↔ super-ux ids)

nodes.label: Frame naming SCR-NN/<Screen>/<state> — the backbone
nodes.rationale: Exactly the states listed in that screen's States table — no more, no fewer: a missing frame for a listed state is drift, a frame with no state row is an orphan.

nodes.label: Page order (Cover, Index, Design system, one page per flow, Scratch)
nodes.norm_label: page order (cover, index, design system, one page per flow, scratch)

nodes.label: Variables as tokens — primitive → semantic → component
nodes.rationale: Components reference semantic tokens, never raw values; auto layout on every container is what makes frames translate to real layout code.
nodes.norm_label: variables as tokens — primitive → semantic → component

nodes.label: What the agent checks (frame parity, orphans, token references)
nodes.rationale: get_metadata is the cheap read that confirms a frame still exists under its expected name without pulling full design context; get_variable_defs makes 'built on the tokens' checkable rather than assumed.
nodes.norm_label: what the agent checks (frame parity, orphans, token references)

nodes.label: What travels and what does not (invariant vs reconsidered per locale)
nodes.rationale: Some of a voice is invariant and some has to be decided again per language; the difference has to be written down or every locale quietly becomes its own brand. Address form changes perception more than any word choice.
nodes.norm_label: what travels and what does not (invariant vs reconsidered per locale)

nodes.label: Length coefficient (multiplies every field limit per locale)
nodes.rationale: The tightest surfaces break first; a 30-character App Store title at 1.3 leaves 23 characters of meaning — a design constraint on the English original, not a translation problem discovered later.
nodes.norm_label: length coefficient (multiplies every field limit per locale)

nodes.label: Translate the job the string does, not the words (B072)
nodes.rationale: The primary locale is the source of meaning, not of form: a word-for-word CTA is grammatically perfect and nobody clicks it. The shorter the string, the more its impact depends on idiom.
nodes.norm_label: translate the job the string does, not the words (b072)

nodes.label: Parity declared rather than hidden (B071)
nodes.rationale: A partial locale that declares itself is a known state; one that does not is a surprise waiting for a user who does not speak the fallback.

nodes.label: Keywords are researched per market, never translated
nodes.rationale: The translation of a high-volume English keyword is routinely a term with no volume; if the market's questions differ, the headings differ too.
nodes.norm_label: keywords are researched per market, never translated

nodes.label: Marketing copy — pages, posts and long form
nodes.norm_label: marketing copy — pages, posts and long form

nodes.label: Four inputs before writing (action, reader, their words, proof)
nodes.rationale: Copy that names the problem in the reader's words outperforms copy that names it in the company's, and the gap is not close.
nodes.community_name: UI Copy Laws and AI Tells
nodes.norm_label: four inputs before writing (action, reader, their words, proof)

nodes.label: Page structure (headline → final CTA) and page types
nodes.rationale: One idea per section — a section that advances two arguments advances neither.
nodes.norm_label: page structure (headline → final cta) and page types

nodes.label: The seven sweeps (clarity → zero risk)
nodes.rationale: Run in order, re-checking earlier sweeps after each one because a fix in one dimension routinely breaks an earlier one. Emotion that replaces the argument is manipulation and out of bounds.

nodes.label: The grounding model (prerequisite vs introduced)
nodes.rationale: A passage that reaches for an ungrounded concept loses the reader, and the loss is silent; the unit is the concept, not the word, so a paragraph can lean on an idea the reader lacks with no jargon in sight.

nodes.label: Comparison-page honesty rule (concede something real)
nodes.rationale: A comparison with no line naming what the competitor does better is read as an advertisement and discounted entirely — the concession is what makes the rest credible.

nodes.label: Search and answer engines — safety first
nodes.norm_label: search and answer engines — safety first

nodes.label: The absolute rule — no fabricated facts, quotes, statistics or experts
nodes.rationale: The GEO24 visibility lift from fabricated citations is a closed window: fabrication is now trained against as an adversarial signal, it creates FTC §5 exposure, and the lift evaporates under competition (C-SEO Bench, NeurIPS 2025). Real evidence in the same structural patterns captures most of the effect with none of the risk.
nodes.norm_label: the absolute rule — no fabricated facts, quotes, statistics or experts

nodes.label: The safety veto list (blocked crawlers, clickbait mismatch, no byline)
nodes.rationale: Any veto caps the value of everything else on the page; a page that is optimized and unsafe is a liability that also stops working, so safety precedes optimization by order, not preference.
nodes.norm_label: the safety veto list (blocked crawlers, clickbait mismatch, no byline)

nodes.label: Optimization — structure that makes content extractable
nodes.rationale: Extraction is structural: position weighting decays sharply, and a sentence that needs the previous paragraph to make sense cannot be quoted, and therefore is not.
nodes.norm_label: optimization — structure that makes content extractable

nodes.label: Technical floor (robots.txt, no-JS rendering, semantic HTML, schema)
nodes.rationale: Declaring AI search as a target while blocking GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot is the contradiction B050 exists to catch.
nodes.norm_label: technical floor (robots.txt, no-js rendering, semantic html, schema)

nodes.label: Store listings — App Store and Google Play
nodes.norm_label: store listings — app store and google play

nodes.label: Store field limits and the two structural differences
nodes.rationale: App Store has a hidden keyword field while Google Play indexes the description, so the two descriptions are written for different readers; promotional text is the only field changeable between releases, which makes it the place for anything time-bound.
nodes.norm_label: store field limits and the two structural differences

nodes.label: The iOS keyword field (B041 — four rules)
nodes.rationale: 100 characters and most listings waste a third: no space after commas, no plurals, nothing already in the title or subtitle, no competitor brand names (grounds for rejection, not a style preference).
nodes.norm_label: the ios keyword field (b041 — four rules)

nodes.label: Screenshot captions name the outcome, not the UI
nodes.rationale: The caption is read before the screenshot is understood, so it carries the value; the first screenshot does the work of a headline.

nodes.label: Composition gates (0.32.0)
nodes.rationale: A structural audit of 0.31.0 found twenty-two defects that 3427 green checks could not see, because the suite verified shape and never once verified composition. Each finding class was turned into a check that fails, rather than a ledger entry.

nodes.label: validate_stated_numbers
nodes.rationale: Recomputes every count written in prose against the artifact it counts; introduced because 181 practices vs a catalog of 206 and '31 deterministic checks' vs a linter emitting 33 had agreed with themselves for months.

nodes.label: validate_skill_parity
nodes.rationale: Asks for each skill by name in five places — its directory, a Cursor rule, the system map, both manifest descriptions, and commands/ux.md — because absence has one side and no single file looks wrong.

nodes.label: validate_seeded_scripts
nodes.rationale: Proves every script an instruction names is copied there by some command; three commands told the reader to run a script nothing installed.

nodes.label: validate_brand_lint_coverage
nodes.rationale: Every code the brand linter can emit must have a fixture and a contract row — four codes had shipped with no fixture while the suite was green and the count looked right.

nodes.label: validate_catalog()
nodes.rationale: The catalog's shape — five fields per entry, unbroken ids, taxonomy tags, and every practice reachable from practice-selection.md — was an invariant held by hand. A practice no skill routes to is a practice that does not exist.

nodes.label: sync_references.py — transitive closure of skill links
nodes.rationale: The skills CLI ships only a skill's own directory, so shared contracts arrived dangling on non-Claude agents. Copying the transitive closure fixes that, but one link from system-map.md to brand-contract.md put all nine brand contracts inside every UX skill — so the map names contracts and links none.
nodes.norm_label: sync_references.py — transitive closure of skill links

nodes.label: brand-contract v1
nodes.rationale: docs/brand/ is a second artifact root beside docs/ux/ on purpose: the brand also governs surfaces that are not UX at all — a store listing, an ad, a post. The pack derives from foundation.md and never the reverse.

nodes.label: ux-contract v4
nodes.rationale: Stays v4 across several releases because every added section (product mechanics, telemetry, kill criteria, vision.md) is optional and additive — no existing docs/ux file changes shape and there is nothing to migrate.

nodes.label: vision skill and /vision
nodes.rationale: Foundation answers who uses the product and why; vision answers what the product IS and refuses to become. Shipped in 0.31.0 connected to nothing, and wired into the map, linter, doctor, templates and /ux-init in 0.32.0.

nodes.label: brand-voice skill
nodes.rationale: Defines and holds the identity; invoked with no task it reports state and proposes exactly one next action, and never invents a missing fact to close a gap.

nodes.label: copywriting skill
nodes.rationale: Writes in the voice and never writes to it — a missing term or an unsourced number is reported, because adding it is brand-voice's decision.

nodes.label: ux-audit skill
nodes.rationale: Gains scope copy — the judgement twin of the brand linter — plus a REFINE/REDESIGN/NEW verdict, because findings alone read as a to-do list and a surface that should be rebuilt gets patched indefinitely.

nodes.label: brand_lint.py — 33 deterministic checks
nodes.rationale: Seeded as docs/brand/lint.py; codes B001–B073 across contract, terminology, string consistency, facts, channel physics, bot safety, machine-drafting markers and locales. Four defects only surfaced when it was pointed at real prose.

nodes.label: ux_lint.py deterministic linter
nodes.rationale: Turns the prose rules into a check that fails: missing Figma frames per state, flows referencing non-existent SCR-IDs, unresolved traces, must/should stories without scenarios, orphan screens, index desync, broken links.

nodes.label: ux_doctor.py contract doctor
nodes.rationale: ux_lint checks a chain against itself, so a base written entirely to an old contract passes it — from the inside such a chain is consistent. The doctor checks it against the contract instead.

nodes.label: UI Screen Registry (screens.md)
nodes.rationale: One entry per screen with a stable SCR-NN id and every state carrying its own Figma frame link; flows reference screens by ID instead of duplicating specs, so a screen used by many flows is described once.

nodes.label: Style pack — one locked visual identity
nodes.rationale: super-ux decided what every screen must contain and left the look to be invented frame by frame — the visual half of the drift it exists to prevent. One pack is recorded once and obeyed everywhere; two identities are worse than any one.
nodes.norm_label: style pack — one locked visual identity

nodes.label: Practice Selection Protocol
nodes.rationale: The deterministic bridge from product profile to mandatory consideration sets to per-artifact checklists to a compliance table with verdicts. Consideration is mandatory; adoption only when a traced job is served — no silent skips, no cargo cult.

nodes.label: best-practices.md catalog (BP-NNN)
nodes.rationale: A living, tag-indexed catalog where each practice carries Do / Why / Apply when / Tags / Source. Figures that did not survive a check were dropped rather than repeated.

nodes.label: Figma integration surface
nodes.rationale: Opt-in but on by default; frames named SCR-NN/<Screen>/<state> map 1:1 to screens.md so lookup is deterministic and drift is checkable. The MCP gates its own tools behind guidance skills, and skipping those gates is the server's documented cause of hard-to-debug failures.

nodes.label: UX plan (docs/ux/plans/)
nodes.rationale: Target interface per screen plus a traced CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE table prioritized by Frequency × Severity × Solvability — written to be executable without the conversation that produced it.

nodes.label: Audit depth levels quick/standard/deep
nodes.rationale: A batched audit reads a slice of the code, so silence about the rest was being read as coverage; a required 'Scope and limits' section now states that absence from a report never means PASS.

nodes.label: One owner per fact
nodes.rationale: A field, rule or path is defined in exactly one file and referenced everywhere else. Design system moved out of foundation.md because it contradicted screens.md; two definitions is drift with a delay fuse.

nodes.label: Explicit build gate before interface code
nodes.rationale: Do not write interface code until the chain is designed and approved and (Figma on) every screen is linked to its frame — stated plainly to a user who is not expected to know the internals.
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules
nodes.norm_label: explicit build gate before interface code

nodes.label: Six shipped voice packs with declared degeneration
nodes.rationale: Each pack declares the degeneration it collapses into when overdone, so an overshoot is a finding rather than a matter of taste.
nodes.norm_label: six shipped voice packs with declared degeneration

nodes.label: best-practices-index.md generated tag index
nodes.rationale: Generated by bp_index.py over a catalog past the point of being read whole; the validator fails when the index drifts from the catalog.

nodes.label: 0.27.0 tagged from a stale base
nodes.rationale: The 0.27.0 tag was pushed from a tree predating 0.26.2–0.26.5, so the GitHub release was missing four merged changes. A clean tree and a green validator say nothing about whether the remote moved while you worked.

nodes.label: A rule must be installed where the running agent reads
nodes.rationale: The ported vision generator wrote its guardian rule to a hardcoded .cursor/skills/ path; it now installs into whichever instruction file the project uses, because a rule the agent cannot see is worse than no rule — absence looks identical to compliance.
nodes.norm_label: a rule must be installed where the running agent reads

nodes.label: UX scenarios hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: scenarios.md is the source of truth for user-facing behavior; every change updates scenarios, flows and screens in the same change. A screen whose code diverges from its record, or a stale Figma link, is the exact drift the system prevents.
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules

nodes.label: Brand voice hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: Never quote a number with no row in facts.md; one action keeps one name across every surface; no humor, exclamation marks or emoji on error, destructive-confirm, billing or paywall surfaces, in any voice.

nodes.label: Vision alignment hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: Check a new capability against the anti-vision and the alignment test before planning; on conflict name the layer, offer reshape-or-amend, and wait. Deliberately does NOT fire on bug fixes, refactors or docs — a vision check on a typo fix is how a team learns to skip the check that matters.

nodes.label: Run each gate alone and read its own exit code
nodes.rationale: Never pipe a validator: tail exits 0 whatever it reads, so 'validate.py | tail -2 && git commit' commits on a red validator. That happened once, in this family, on a tag.
nodes.norm_label: run each gate alone and read its own exit code

nodes.label: A skill exists in seven places or it does not exist
nodes.rationale: Its own directory, a cursor/rules/<name>.mdc, the system map's skill list, both manifest descriptions, and commands/ux.md so /ux can route to it. Absence has one side and no single file looks wrong.
nodes.norm_label: a skill exists in seven places or it does not exist

nodes.label: A hard rule has one source text in templates/
nodes.rationale: The rule's text lives in templates/ and the installing command carries an identical embedded copy, paired in HARD_RULES. A rule with two texts is the drift this plugin exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: a hard rule has one source text in templates/

nodes.label: Every link in a skill is a shipping instruction
nodes.rationale: sync_references.py copies the transitive closure of a skill's links into that skill, so one link from system-map.md to brand-contract.md once put all nine brand contracts inside every UX skill. The map names contracts; it links none.
nodes.norm_label: every link in a skill is a shipping instruction

nodes.label: Why the contracts are duplicated per skill
nodes.rationale: The skills CLI ships only a skill's own directory, so a sibling skills/references/ arrives dangling on every non-Claude agent. skills/references/ is the source of truth; the per-skill copies are generated and must stay byte-identical — never edit a copy by hand.
nodes.norm_label: why the contracts are duplicated per skill

nodes.label: The edit → sync → validate loop
nodes.rationale: validate.py is the gate CI runs on every push and PR. If you add a rule to the methodology, add the check that fails when someone breaks it — a prose rule nobody can verify is a suggestion.

nodes.label: validate_stated_numbers invariant
nodes.rationale: Every count written in prose equals the artifact it counts. The README advertised 181 practices against a catalog of 206 and 31 lint checks against 33, for months, with a green suite.

nodes.label: validate_skill_parity invariant
nodes.rationale: A skill exists in five places or it does not exist; adding a skill without adding its Cursor rule fails here.

nodes.label: validate_seeded_scripts invariant
nodes.rationale: A hard rule that says 'run python3 docs/brand/lint.py' while nothing installs that file is the defect this catches.

nodes.label: One owner per fact (convention)
nodes.rationale: A field, rule or path is defined in exactly one file and referenced everywhere else. Two definitions is drift with a delay fuse — several past bugs were exactly this.

nodes.label: Stable IDs, never reused
nodes.rationale: SCN-NNN, FLW-NN, SCR-NN, ST-NNN, BP-NNN, PRN-NN; retired entries stay with a reason so a reference never silently re-points.

nodes.label: Never stamp a Checked date you did not earn
nodes.rationale: The field exists to make staleness visible; a date written to fill a column reports a verification nobody performed and is worse than no field at all. BP-001..181 carry none by decision.
nodes.norm_label: never stamp a checked date you did not earn

nodes.label: release_preflight.py
nodes.rationale: Fetches and refuses when HEAD does not contain origin/main — v0.27.0 shipped from a base four releases old for exactly that reason.

nodes.label: git push --atomic origin main vX.Y.Z
nodes.rationale: --follow-tags is not atomic: a rejected branch still lets the tag through, and CI will build a release from it.

nodes.label: The family catalogue moves with the release
nodes.rationale: sshlg-skills pins every member's version in skills.json; a release that does not bump that pin is invisible — list keeps reporting the previous version and update keeps installing it, with nothing to reveal the mismatch.
nodes.norm_label: the family catalogue moves with the release

nodes.label: Test from a packed tarball, not the working tree
nodes.rationale: The repo is not the artifact — npm pack into a temp dir and run the installer there, then confirm the seeded project lints clean from the first second. A files[] omission is invisible from the working tree.

nodes.norm_label: test from a packed tarball, not the working tree

nodes.label: The design chain (vision → foundation → flows → screens → scenarios)
nodes.rationale: A versioned chain in docs/ux/ becomes the source of truth, written and approved before UI exists and updated in the same change as any behavior change. Every layer traces to the one above it.
nodes.norm_label: the design chain (vision → foundation → flows → screens → scenarios)

nodes.label: The hard rule installed into CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Coding agents write UI without a model of user behavior, so the process is fixed rather than the symptom: the rule makes the chain non-optional at the point where code would otherwise be written.
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules
nodes.norm_label: the hard rule installed into claude.md

nodes.label: Do not write interface code until the chain is approved
nodes.rationale: Building UI before the chain is designed, approved and (with Figma on) mocked up is the mistake super-ux exists to prevent.
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules
nodes.norm_label: do not write interface code until the chain is approved

nodes.label: The brand layer — docs/brand/
nodes.rationale: docs/ux/ decides what the product does; docs/brand/ decides how it speaks. A linter makes copy drift as findable as chain drift, but clean means checkable, not good — tone judgement stays with /ux-audit copy.

nodes.label: Style pack recorded in screens.md → Design system
nodes.rationale: One locked pack is the identity for the whole product; inventing a palette, type pairing or motion per screen is visual drift.
nodes.norm_label: style pack recorded in screens.md → design system

nodes.label: Craft floors vs style pack identity
nodes.rationale: BP-079..090 and BP-130..135 are floors (contrast, line length, tap targets, spacing rhythm, motion tokens, reduced motion, narrow viewport) and always win on safety; the style pack owns identity and wins on look. Both decisions land in the compliance table.
nodes.norm_label: craft floors vs style pack identity

nodes.label: sheleg-design companion
nodes.rationale: Recommended, never required, and offered once: super-ux owns structure and behavior and deliberately stops at the visual edge.

nodes.label: task-pipeline companion
nodes.rationale: Picks up after an audit or Improve pass produced a UX plan and executes it through gated stages; the user still owns how they finish.

nodes.label: /ux — the one command
nodes.rationale: Reports status across every layer then offers only the applicable actions with one marked recommended; the user never picks a skill or a layer, because a skill the entry point cannot route to is a skill nobody runs.

nodes.label: docs/ux/lint.py + /ux-lint
nodes.rationale: The deterministic half of drift detection — stdlib-only, exit 1 on problems, meant for CI so drift cannot merge.
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules

nodes.label: docs/brand/lint.py (33 checks B001..B073)
nodes.rationale: Catches banned words, one action under two names, a figure with no sourced fact, a field over its locale-adjusted limit, blocked AI crawlers, keyword stuffing, humor on a billing screen, a lagging locale.

nodes.label: system-map.md
nodes.rationale: The whole system on one page — pipeline, files, skills, companions and the four sync rules; every skill points here so an agent entering from any trigger sees the whole system.

nodes.label: docs/ux/doctor.py + /ux-doctor
nodes.community_name: The Build Gate and Hard Rules

nodes.label: A plain skills copy shadows the plugin
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit --agent list the skills CLI detects Claude Code and re-creates ~/.claude/skills/<skill> as a plain copy, which serves its frozen version forever. Nothing reports it: the plugin updates, the copy does not, and the copy is what loads.

nodes.label: Practice Selection Protocol
nodes.rationale: A deterministic bridge between the practice catalogs and the two functions that consume them (design and audit), so the right practices get considered at the right step every time — nothing relevant silently skipped, nothing irrelevant cargo-culted.

nodes.label: Step 1 — Product profile
nodes.rationale: Built once from foundation.md across nine dimensions (platform, money model, distribution, purchase surface, acquisition, forms, analytics, personalization, engagement mechanics); missing dimensions are asked of the user and stored back in the foundation so selection is reproducible.

nodes.label: Step 2 — Mandatory consideration sets
nodes.rationale: 'Mandatory consideration' means each practice in the set gets an explicit verdict, not automatic adoption. PRN-01..24 and BP-001 apply to every product; PRN-22..24 read as brand rules and are therefore easy to file as optional, but any product with text has them — which is every product with an interface.

nodes.label: Step 3 — Per-artifact checklists
nodes.rationale: Forty artifact rows (onboarding, paywall, trial, cancel, forms, growth loop, landing, pricing, dunning, web2app, navigation, strings, error states, store listing, accessibility pass, gamified surface, …) pulled ON TOP of the Step-2 sets when designing or auditing one specific flow.

nodes.label: Step 4 — Compliance table (the record)
nodes.rationale: Verdicts are applied / adapted (how) / rejected (a reason, not a shrug) / deferred (what unblocks it). applied and adapted must be visible in the artifact — a verdict without a trace is fiction. Rejections owned by the user (taste, brand, strategy) are recorded as such and NOT re-litigated on every pass.

nodes.label: Anti-cargo-cult rule
nodes.rationale: A practice is applied only when it serves a traced job/story of THIS product. The mandatory sets force the consideration, never the adoption. When two practices conflict, the foundation's Monetization section decides, and the conflict plus decision goes into the compliance table.

nodes.label: Style pack vs practices precedence
nodes.rationale: The style pack owns identity (palette, type pairing, motion tokens, bans) and wins on look; the practices own floors (contrast, tap targets, line length, spacing rhythm) and win on safety. Any conflict and its resolution is recorded in the compliance table like any other.

nodes.label: Visual craft (BP-079..090)
nodes.rationale: Typography, color and layout floors that apply to any graphical UI; the concrete palette/type/motion come from the recorded style pack, not from these.

nodes.label: Trend governance & perceived quality (BP-145..146, BP-165..172)
nodes.rationale: A trend is adopted through its named mechanism with the compensation stated; defaults that read as generated are a quality tell.

nodes.label: Eight-step design pipeline (RESEARCH → VERIFY)
nodes.rationale: RESEARCH, DEFINE, STRUCTURE, MAP, SPECIFY, VISUALIZE, BUILD UI, VERIFY — BUILD UI is step 7 on purpose: it is the only step whose early execution invalidates the six before it.

nodes.label: Forward mode (new product or feature)
nodes.rationale: Run steps 1→7 in order: never design a screen before its flow exists, never draw a flow for a story that traces to no job.

nodes.label: Backwards mode (existing product)
nodes.rationale: Fill the same artifacts in reverse — inventory UI → reconstruct flows → derive scenarios → infer stories/jobs — tagging every reverse-engineered entry `inferred` until a human confirms; the gaps between 'is' and 'should' become the improvement backlog.

nodes.label: Task analysis method
nodes.rationale: Decompose a story into user-visible micro-steps, then ask of each whether it serves the job, whether the system can do it instead, and whether two steps collapse; mark where the user first receives real value — aha is engineered, not hoped for.

nodes.label: Flow design rules
nodes.rationale: One flow = one user goal; every decision an explicit branch; every error edge lands somewhere recoverable (dead ends are defects by definition); all entry points enumerated because flows entered mid-way must still work; happy-path steps above five get challenged.

nodes.label: Screen & interaction rules
nodes.rationale: Exactly one primary action per screen; undo beats confirmation when both are possible; empty states sell the next action; accessibility, motion and responsiveness are decided in text at spec time, not retrofitted — an effect with no reduced-motion branch is unfinished, not polished.

nodes.label: Nielsen heuristics checklist (PRN-01..PRN-10)
nodes.rationale: Each heuristic carries an audit question so a violation can be cited by principle ID as evidence rather than asserted as taste.

nodes.label: Motivation principles (PRN-17..PRN-21)
nodes.rationale: Goal-gradient, Zeigarnik, IKEA, endowment and zero-price describe why a user keeps going; recorded as `applied` each must name which side of the honesty line it sits on and what the user gets from it.

nodes.label: The coercive twin (honesty stance)
nodes.rationale: Every motivation lever has a twin aimed at the product's interest instead of the user's. A mechanism that only works while the user misunderstands the situation is a dark pattern wearing a principle's name: applied honestly the levers make a real goal easier to reach, applied otherwise they manufacture a goal the user never had.

nodes.label: Voice principles (PRN-22..PRN-24)
nodes.rationale: They sit beside the interaction principles rather than under them: a product can satisfy every heuristic and still read like three different companies. Recorded as `applied` they must name the surface and the voice pack judged against, since a voice judged with no recorded pack is judged against taste.

nodes.label: PRN-20 — Endowment
nodes.rationale: Honest use is a full-featured trial that shows the real product; the coercive use grants then removes capability to create a loss the user did not choose.

nodes.label: PRN-24 — Never joke about the user's loss

nodes.label: Heuristic evaluation procedure (improving existing UX)
nodes.rationale: Requires a backwards-mode chain first — you cannot judge UX without knowing the intended jobs. Every redesign proposal traces to a pain/job/story, cites PRN-NN or BP-NNN, shows before → after flows and states the expected observable effect; 'make it prettier' is not a proposal.

nodes.label: Anti-patterns (stop signals)
nodes.rationale: Screens before flows; a flow node with no error edge; copying a mechanic without naming its mechanism; adopting a look because it is current (a trend with no mechanism, owner or review date is debt on arrival); treating accessibility, motion or page weight as post-build polish; optimizing a step that shouldn't exist; treating the paywall as exempt from honesty rules — dark patterns create churn and refunds, not LTV.

nodes.label: UX Contract v4
nodes.rationale: THE contract for docs/ux/ in a target project, followed by the vision, ux-foundation, ux-flows, ux-scenarios and ux-audit skills and the Cursor rules. Field names, ID schemes, statuses and verdicts must not be deviated from because tooling and audits key off them.

nodes.label: The chain: Personas → Jobs → Journeys → Stories → Flows → Screens → Scenarios → Audits → Plans
nodes.rationale: Every layer traces to the one above it. foundation.md, flows.md and screens.md are optional for tiny projects (v1 mode, scenarios alone), but once a layer exists its traceability and same-change rules apply; in backwards mode the same files are filled in reverse from code, entries tagged `inferred` until confirmed.
nodes.norm_label: the chain: personas → jobs → journeys → stories → flows → screens → scenarios → audits → plans

nodes.label: Same-change update rule (all layers)
nodes.rationale: Scenarios always; flows when navigation/branches/errors change; screens.md whenever elements, states or coverage change — and with Figma on, the frame updated and its link re-verified in the same change. A screen whose code diverges from its record, or a stale/broken Figma link, is a `drifted` finding, not an acceptable state.

nodes.label: Scenario `Strings:` field (optional)
nodes.rationale: Lists strings.md keys (not text — the text lives in one place) so a copy audit can walk from a scenario to the exact strings serving it, and brand_lint.py can tell a string that serves a real scenario from one nobody claims. Its absence is never an error.

nodes.label: docs/ux/vision.md contract — nine sections
nodes.rationale: Optional and owned by the vision skill; present or absent, never partial — a vision missing its anti-vision is the one shape that reliably settles no argument. It is a gate, not a document: without the hard-rule block in the project's instruction file it is a file nothing reads. foundation.md must not contradict it; a contradiction is a finding to raise, not to smooth over.

nodes.label: Two layers answer a "what" question
nodes.rationale: vision.md says what the product IS; scenarios.md says what it DOES. Never merge them: a feature can satisfy every scenario and still violate the anti-vision, and that is precisely the case the vision layer exists to catch.

nodes.label: Personas (P-NN)
nodes.rationale: Validation bar: recognizable by a real user ('does this sound like you?'), grounded in data or observation, not invented traits.

nodes.label: Jobs to Be Done (JTBD-NN)
nodes.rationale: Statement, personas, type (functional/emotional/social), the four forces (push, pull, anxiety, habit) and a success metric that is an observable user outcome, not a feature.

nodes.label: Customer journeys (JRN-NN)
nodes.rationale: One journey per persona × job that matters, staged end-to-end (before, during, after the product), each row carrying touchpoint, emotion, pain and opportunity; opportunity priority = Frequency × Severity × Solvability.

nodes.label: User stories (ST-NNN)
nodes.rationale: Quality bar is INVEST; acceptance criteria are Given/When/Then and observable; status runs proposed → validated → delivered → dropped.

nodes.label: Kill criteria (optional story field)
nodes.rationale: Records before the work starts the signal that would say the bet was wrong — a metric, a threshold, a date, and what happens when it is missed. `dropped` exists as a status that nothing ever defines, so it is only reached by someone losing interest, the slowest possible way to learn. A story that cannot name a signal that would retire it is usually a story nobody can evaluate at all.

nodes.label: Monetization model section
nodes.rationale: Model, value metric, free boundary, purchase surface, money moments and acquisition coherence. Money moments are inputs to flows.md: each gets a first-class flow, not an afterthought edge; with web checkout or web2app the funnel and the paid handoff are flows of this product too, held to the same rigor as in-app screens.

nodes.label: Design tooling section (Figma on/off + file URL)
nodes.rationale: Exactly two fields — the on/off choice and the file location. The design system (library, tokens, component source, assets) belongs to screens.md → Design system: one owner per fact, never both.
nodes.norm_label: design tooling section (figma on/off + file url)

nodes.label: Product mechanics section (personalization, engagement, accessibility regime)
nodes.rationale: Three facts the practice-selection profile reads and cannot infer from the rest of the chain; an absent section means all three unstated, treated as `none`. Each recorded mechanic carries consequences into flows.md — an engagement mechanic owes a recovery flow, personalization owes a correction path, a stated regime owes its checks in every scenario's UI elements.
nodes.norm_label: product mechanics section (personalization, engagement, accessibility regime)

nodes.label: ID rules (sequential, never reused)
nodes.rationale: P-NN, JTBD-NN, JRN-NN, ST-NNN, FLW-NN, SCR-NN, SCN-NNN are sequential and never reused; dropped or retired entries are kept with a status note, never deleted, so an ID in an old audit always resolves.

nodes.label: docs/ux/flows.md (FLW-NN, the HOW layer)
nodes.rationale: One entry per user goal with traces, goal, entry points, success exit, task analysis, a mermaid flowchart and a screens-traversed table. The flow references screens by SCR-ID; a screen used by several flows is described in exactly one place.

nodes.label: Flow rules (node naming, entry points, error edges)
nodes.rationale: Screens as `Screen: <name>`, decisions as diamonds, errors as `*_err` nodes with a labeled recovery edge — an error edge that goes nowhere is a defect; happy-path steps above five need justification.
nodes.norm_label: flow rules (node naming, entry points, error edges)

nodes.label: docs/ux/screens.md — the UI map (SCR-NN)
nodes.rationale: The canonical record of every screen and state: index, design system block, then one entry per screen with purpose, elements (one primary action marked), a row per state with its Figma frame, wireframe, coverage, scenarios and resources. Every state — including empty/error/loading — gets a row; a state without a frame is an incomplete-design finding. Orphans in either direction (screen with no flow, flow screen not recorded) are findings.

nodes.label: screens.md → Design system block
nodes.rationale: Style pack, Figma library, tokens in code, component source and assets recorded ONCE here and referenced everywhere else; the style pack names the visual identity every frame and every built screen obeys.

nodes.label: Screen status lifecycle (designed → built → drifted → retired)
nodes.norm_label: screen status lifecycle (designed → built → drifted → retired)

nodes.label: docs/ux/scenarios.md (SCN-NNN, source of truth for behavior)
nodes.rationale: Ordered structure: managed-by header comment, an index row per scenario, personas (a pointer to foundation.md when it exists, defined inline in v1 mode), then scenarios grouped by feature.
nodes.norm_label: docs/ux/scenarios.md (scn-nnn, source of truth for behavior)

nodes.label: Scenario entry format
nodes.rationale: A scenario is a use case: each numbered step pairs one user action with the system's observable response. Traces are required where the layer exists — a scenario that serves nothing is a candidate for deletion, not implementation. Expected results are observable ('project appears in the sidebar', not 'record inserted'); UI elements are what the audit checks for; 'nothing can fail' must be stated explicitly.

nodes.label: Scenario `Telemetry:` field (optional)
nodes.rationale: Names the analytics event a scenario emits, as object_action snake_case with the verb last and consistent tense, plus the parameters that let it be segmented. This is the bridge the chain was missing: the frustration-telemetry and funnel-measurement practices assume events exist, and nothing tied a named event to the behavior it measures — so the moment a step is renamed, the dashboard silently measures something else.

nodes.label: Scenario lifecycle (draft → validated → implemented → retired)
nodes.rationale: validated requires human approval, implemented requires an audit PASS, and changed scenarios drop back to draft — status cannot advance by assertion.

nodes.label: Traceability rules (per existing layer)
nodes.rationale: Every must/should story has ≥1 flow and ≥1 scenario; every flow node and edge is covered; every scenario traces to ≥1 story or job; every journey stage with a touchpoint has ≥1 scenario. Orphans in either direction are findings, never silently ignored.

nodes.label: Audit report format (docs/ux/audits/YYYY-MM-DD.md)
nodes.rationale: Scope, depth, method, base git SHA, summary totals, per-batch scenario verdicts with file:line evidence, a findings register, scope and limits, the verdict, and — on deep runs — the practice compliance table.

nodes.label: Scenario verdicts (PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL / BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: A verdict without file:line evidence must be BLOCKED, not PASS — the rule that keeps an audit from converting absence of evidence into confirmation.

nodes.label: Finding severity (critical / major / minor)
nodes.rationale: critical = user cannot complete the job or data loss; major = the flow completes but the experience is broken or dishonest; minor = polish.

nodes.label: Scope and limits section (not optional)
nodes.rationale: An audit runs in batches and reads a finite slice of the code, so silence about the rest reads as coverage: absence of a scenario from the report never means PASS. Naming what was left out, what could not be verified and what the code cannot answer is what separates a report from an impression.

nodes.label: The verdict fork — REFINE / REDESIGN / NEW
nodes.rationale: Findings alone always read as a to-do list, so an audit can return dozens and still leave the real question unasked. REFINE = the design is right and the gaps are defects; REDESIGN = the findings cluster on one artifact whose structure causes them and patching will not converge; NEW = the chain does not describe what was built. Without this fork, a surface that should be rebuilt is patched indefinitely, one true finding at a time, and every round looks like progress.
nodes.norm_label: the verdict fork — refine / redesign / new

nodes.label: Practice compliance table (deep audits)
nodes.rationale: Follows the practice-selection protocol, adding the audit-only verdict `missing` (applicable but absent → suggestion finding) to applied / adapted / rejected / deferred.

nodes.label: Coverage audit (scope: coverage)
nodes.rationale: Audits the chain instead of the code — orphan stories, orphan scenarios, journey stages without scenarios, jobs without stories, unused personas — using the same report format with findings referencing layer IDs.

nodes.label: UX plan (docs/ux/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<scope>.md)
nodes.rationale: The actionable output of an audit or Improve pass — target interface per screen plus a CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE change table — written so an autonomous agent can execute it without the conversation. Every row traces to a scenario, flow, finding or principle ID; an untraced change doesn't enter the plan; DELETE rows carry the reason. The plan supersedes nothing: scenarios and flows stay the source of truth.

nodes.label: task-pipeline handoff (recommended, not forced)
nodes.rationale: The plan lists what the user already has and then offers one autonomous path (a 9-stage gated pipeline) with its one-time install; superpowers writing-plans or hand implementation are stated as equally valid. Nothing here forces a tool.

A feature can be perfectly scenario'd and still violate the anti-vision, which is why the alignment check runs before the chain, not inside it.

nodes.label: UX scenarios — hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: The block installed into a target project's instruction file; templates/ is the only source of the hard-rule text, and the command that installs it carries an identical embedded copy so a rule never has two texts.

nodes.label: Do NOT write interface code until the chain is done
nodes.rationale: The foundation → flows → screens → scenarios chain must be designed and approved, and with Figma enabled every screen mocked up and linked to its frame, first. Building UI before this is the exact mistake super-ux exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: do not write interface code until the chain is done

nodes.label: Visual identity is ONE locked style pack
nodes.rationale: Recorded in screens.md → Design system and obeyed by every Figma frame and every built screen; inventing a palette, type pairing or motion per screen is visual drift.
nodes.norm_label: visual identity is one locked style pack

nodes.label: Brand voice — hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: Any change to public-facing text updates docs/brand/ in the same change — a new string with no registry row is drift, not a detail.

nodes.label: Never quote a number with no row in facts.md
nodes.rationale: And never invent a fact, statistic, quote or expert to fill a gap — report the gap instead.
nodes.norm_label: never quote a number with no row in facts.md

nodes.label: One action keeps one name
nodes.rationale: Across button, confirmation, toast, history, notification and accessible name; search strings.md before naming one.

nodes.label: No humor, exclamation marks or emoji where the user can lose something
nodes.rationale: Applies to error, destructive-confirm, billing and paywall surfaces in any voice — including the playful one.
nodes.norm_label: no humor, exclamation marks or emoji where the user can lose something

nodes.label: Vision alignment — hard rule (super-ux)
nodes.rationale: Before planning any new feature, capability or significant change, check it against vision.md — specifically the anti-vision and the alignment test. Aligned means proceed while naming in one line which part of the vision it serves.

nodes.label: Misaligned protocol — name, offer two paths, wait
nodes.rationale: Stop before writing code: name the conflict quoting the layer it contradicts, offer either reshaping the feature to fit or amending the vision with the cost stated, then wait for the decision. Do not pick one silently — the agent proposes, the human decides which layer moves.
nodes.norm_label: misaligned protocol — name, offer two paths, wait

nodes.label: Do NOT trigger for bug fixes, refactors, tests, docs
nodes.rationale: A vision check on a typo fix is how a team learns to skip the check that matters — the gate is scoped narrowly so it stays credible where it applies.
nodes.norm_label: do not trigger for bug fixes, refactors, tests, docs

nodes.label: vision.md template (nine sections)
nodes.rationale: Owned by the vision skill; the headings and their order are what docs/ux/lint.py keys off. Writing the file is half the job — the other half is the hard-rule block in the project's instruction file, without which nothing ever reads the document.

nodes.label: 1. Essence
nodes.rationale: One sentence with no feature names, UI or technology. Test: would it survive a total rewrite on a different stack? If not, it names an implementation.

nodes.label: 2. Core idea
nodes.rationale: An observation about the world, not a problem statement — X is abundant, Y is scarce, this product bridges the gap. One observation, not a list.

nodes.label: 3. What the system does
nodes.rationale: Continuous behaviour in verbs, not nouns — 'has a dashboard' is not behaviour.

nodes.label: 4. The user's role
nodes.rationale: What the user becomes — directs, judges, decides. If it reads like operating any other tool, go deeper.

nodes.label: 5. Principles
nodes.rationale: Three to five, each 'we do X, not Y' where Y is something a reasonable team would genuinely have picked. A principle with no rejected side is a slogan.

nodes.label: 6. Anti-vision
nodes.rationale: What the product refuses to become, naming the adjacent products it could drift into and saying no to each. This is the layer teams skip and the only one that ever settles an argument.

nodes.label: 7. Horizon
nodes.rationale: Two to three years as a direction, not a roadmap — roadmaps belong in the tracker and go stale in a quarter.

nodes.label: 9. The alignment test
nodes.rationale: Three to five questions any proposed feature must pass — what the hard rule in the instruction file actually runs. A stranger should be able to reject a plausible feature with them.
